subject: Comparison between fscores from mirt and thetaEst from catR package

messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: Comparison between fscores from mirt and thetaEst from catR package
parts:
Hello Phil, 


The other day, I asked you regarding r-package for the ability estimation and ability estimation functions for multidimensional items, you suggested mirtCAT for the same. 
I found, you are using fscores function from mirt package to estimate the ability.
To check whether fscores gives the same estimate as that of thetaEst when given uni-dimensional items I performed following experiment :


data(LSAT7)
LSAT7=expand.table(LSAT7)
mod=mirt(LSAT7, 1,itemtype = '3PL')
fscor=fscores(object = mod,method = "ML",response.pattern = c(1,0,1,0,1),theta_lim = c(-4, 4))
ipar=mod2values(mod)
iparm=cbind(ipar$value[ipar$name == 'a1'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'd'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'g'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'u'])
theta=thetaEst(iparm, x =c(1,0,1,0,1), model = NULL, method = "ML")


theta=thetaEst(iparm, x =c(1,0,1,0,1), model = NULL, method = "ML")
> theta
[1] 1.363227


> fscor=fscores(object = mod,method = "ML",response.pattern = c(1,0,1,0,1),theta_lim = c(-4, 4))
> fscor
     Item.1 Item.2 Item.3 Item.4 Item.5         F1     SE_F1
[1,]      1      0      1      0      1 -0.6551783 0.8619742


Shouldn't I get the same results? If yes, what am I missing here? Because my results are not matching.

If not 1) then how come you have used this function in imputation? 2) what does fscores gives as an output, if not ability estimate? 3) Is there any way to get the ability estimates from the fscores?




Regards,

Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Comparison between fscores from mirt and thetaEst from catR package
parts:
Check the parametrizations. mirt uses the slope-intercept form in all models, while I think catR uses the classical representation. Try passing your model to coef(mod, IRTpars = TRUE) for a better mapping. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Comparison between fscores from mirt and thetaEst from catR package
parts:

Phil

Thanking you,
Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Comparison between fscores from mirt and thetaEst from catR package
parts:
Internally, there's no way to do this since theta_lim is specifying the range of the integration grid, not some maximum and minimum. I'll consider adding this option in the future, but it's easy enough to do just on the user end. E.g., ifelse(abs(score) > 4), score, sign(score) * 4), where score is whatever the returned theta value. Cheers.

Phil

> fscor=fscores(object = mod,method = "ML",response.pattern = c(1,0,1,0,1),theta_lim = c(-4, 4))

     Item.1 Item.2 Item.3 Item.4 Item.5         F1     SE_F1

Check the parametrizations. mirt uses the slope-intercept form in all models, while I think catR uses the classical representation. Try passing your model to coef(mod, IRTpars = TRUE) for a better mapping. Cheers.

Hello Phil, 


The other day, I asked you regarding r-package for the ability estimation and ability estimation functions for multidimensional items, you suggested mirtCAT for the same. 
I found, you are using fscores function from mirt package to estimate the ability.
To check whether fscores gives the same estimate as that of thetaEst when given uni-dimensional items I performed following experiment :


data(LSAT7)
LSAT7=expand.table(LSAT7)
mod=mirt(LSAT7, 1,itemtype = '3PL')
fscor=fscores(object = mod,method = "ML",response.pattern = c(1,0,1,0,1),theta_lim = c(-4, 4))
ipar=mod2values(mod)
iparm=cbind(ipar$value[ipar$name == 'a1'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'd'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'g'], ipar$value[ipar$name == 'u'])
theta=thetaEst(iparm, x =c(1,0,1,0,1), model = NULL, method = "ML")


theta=thetaEst(iparm, x =c(1,0,1,0,1), model = NULL, method = "ML")
> theta
[1] 1.363227


> fscor=fscores(object = mod,method = "ML",response.pattern = c(1,0,1,0,1),theta_lim = c(-4, 4))
> fscor
     Item.1 Item.2 Item.3 Item.4 Item.5         F1     SE_F1
[1,]      1      0      1      0      1 -0.6551783 0.8619742
